novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement relationship: a "fast, early metacognitive 'familiarity' ... computed before and independently of actual content retrieval" that "gates how much retrieval effort is expended," with false-high and false-low familiarity symmetrically causing confabulation and missed recall. Searches for "LLM feeling of knowing before retrieval," "LLM familiarity gates retrieval effort," "internal answerability direction activation steering," and "metacognitive confidence factual recall" identified the closest work as LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It (2026), which uses an explicitly elicited pre-solve FOK signal to control test-time reasoning, alongside Too Late to Recall (2025), KEEN/answerability-direction work, and Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning (2024); none of these establishes a surface-driven internal familiarity representation dissociable from retrieved factual content and causally upstream of retrieval. Moving from those works to the claimed two-signal mechanism and its symmetric miscalibration account requires a new core relationship rather than a direct transfer, although it remains within established metacognition, confidence-steering, and retrieval-versus-storage frameworks rather than creating a new paradigm.
